title: WHO — World Health Organization
shortDescription: The UN's health agency: how it's governed, what it actually does, and how it's structured across regions.
genZNote: Global health's actual chain of command — not just 'the vaccine people'.

sections.heading: Full Form, Establishment, Headquarters
bullets: Established: 7 April 1948 (celebrated annually as World Health Day) — its constitution had been adopted the year before, in 1946.
A UN specialized agency for international public health — not a UN programme/fund.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.body: WHO's constitution states its objective as 'the attainment by all peoples of the highest possible level of health' — defining health broadly as 'a state of complete physical, mental and social well-being and not merely the absence of disease or infirmity'.

rows: WHO's supreme decision-making body — all member states, meets annually in Geneva; sets policy, approves the budget, elects the Director-General.
Gives effect to WHA decisions and policies; members are technically qualified health experts nominated by elected member states, serving 3-year terms.
WHO's chief technical and administrative officer, appointed by the WHA on the Executive Board's nomination, for a 5-year renewable term.
Six regional offices (Africa, Americas, South-East Asia, Europe, Eastern Mediterranean, Western Pacific) — India falls under the South-East Asia Region, headquartered in New Delhi.

sections.heading: Major Functions
bullets: Global disease surveillance and outbreak response coordination.
Setting international health standards and norms (e.g. the International Health Regulations, IHR 2005 — the legal framework for responding to public health emergencies of international concern).
Vaccination/immunization programmes and technical guidance (e.g. the Expanded Programme on Immunization).
Declaring 'Public Health Emergencies of International Concern' (PHEIC) — the highest level of global health alert under the IHR.
Running normative programmes on non-communicable diseases, maternal/child health, mental health, and essential medicines (the WHO Model List of Essential Medicines).

sections.heading: WHO and India
bullets: India is a founding member of WHO (1948) and hosts the WHO Regional Office for South-East Asia in New Delhi.
India was certified polio-free by WHO in 2014, following the last wild poliovirus case in January 2011.

WHO has recognized several India-led global health initiatives, including the push for traditional medicine collaboration (WHO Global Centre for Traditional Medicine, established in Jamnagar, Gujarat).

sections.heading: Current Leadership (time-sensitive — verify before an exam)
sections.body: Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus (Ethiopia) has served as WHO Director-General since 2017, re-elected for a second term beginning August 2022; the WHO's next Director-General election cycle is scheduled for 2026–2027. Because this is a role that changes, always cross-check the current holder close to your exam date rather than memorising a name as permanent.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: WHO is the UN's specialized health agency, established 1948, headquartered in Geneva, governed by the World Health Assembly and an Executive Board, and headed by a Director-General.
keyFacts: Established 7 April 1948 — celebrated as World Health Day.
HQ: Geneva. Six regional offices; India is under the South-East Asia Region (New Delhi).
Supreme body: World Health Assembly (WHA). Executive arm: Director-General.
International Health Regulations (IHR 2005) govern PHEIC declarations.
India declared polio-free by WHO in 2014.
commonConfusion: WHO is a specialized agency (independent, UN-linked by agreement) — it is not a UN programme/fund like UNICEF or UNDP.

highYieldFacts: WHO founded 1948, HQ Geneva, World Health Day = 7 April.
India falls under WHO's South-East Asia Region, headquartered in New Delhi.
India certified polio-free by WHO in 2014.
commonTraps: Do not confuse the World Health Assembly (WHO's policy-setting body) with the Executive Board (which implements WHA decisions) — the WHA is the supreme body, not the Board.
Don't treat WHO's regional office location (New Delhi) as WHO's global headquarters — that's Geneva.
mustRemember: WHO's founding objective: 'the highest possible level of health' for all peoples.
PHEIC declarations are made under the legal authority of the International Health Regulations (2005).
